meta.provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.

lander.name: Nova-C class (IoT estimate)
lander.model: sun-tracking array: power = p_panel x visible Sun fraction, whatever the Sun's direction, so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels

sources.p_load: ESTIMATE from Odysseus lasting 10-20 hours on battery (Reuters)

definitions.safe_landing_date: a day with at least one safe landing hour: touchdown with more than half the Sun and Earth in view, Earth in view for at least 50% of the 14-day mission (no relay), and the battery never below 140 Wh
definitions.ranking: one list per mast height: most safe landing days (safe at every point within 100 m when that check ran; a site with none there stays, below the others), then the most safe days on the site's own point, then the least battery needed
definitions.battery_needed_Wh: the most battery energy any safe landing hour draws: a full charge minus the lowest level during the mission (the battery model, so sunlight that comes back partway counts); at most 560 Wh by the safe rule
definitions.default_mast: 2 m: the best-fit observer height when the engine is checked against NASA's maps
definitions.recommended_mast_m: the shortest mast with at least one safe landing date (information only)
definitions.fields: per-mast numbers are for that mast's headline landing (headline_start): the best one safe within 100 m where that check found one, else the best on the exact point; null if the mast has no safe landing. detail_file is that landing's full mission

profile.label: Nova-C-class lander, 14-day mission
profile.description: The default: a lander like Intuitive Machines' Nova-C (700 Wh battery, 200 W of panels), working for 14 days, with Earth counted as soon as any part of it shows above the horizon.
profile.payloads: Landing sensors (NDL lidar, SCALPSS plume cameras), radio and navigation beacons (LN-1) and power-hungry science (PRIME-1 drill and mass spectrometer), as flown on IM-1 and IM-2.
